items.q: Lan: Where's Nam? / Minh: He ______ for a job interview at the moment, so don't disturb him.
items.vi: Lan: Nam đâu rồi? / Minh: Bạn ấy đang chuẩn bị cho buổi phỏng vấn xin việc lúc này, nên đừng làm phiền.
items.explanation:
At the moment means right now, so the present continuous is preparing describes an action in progress at the time of speaking.
✗ prepares — simple present is for habits and facts, not what is happening now; ✗ has prepared — present perfect means the preparing is finished, but he is still busy; ✗ prepared — past simple puts it in the past, yet 'don't disturb him' shows it is happening now.

items.q: Our garden party was cancelled because of a sudden ______ that flooded the lawn in minutes.
items.vi: Bữa tiệc ngoài vườn của chúng tôi bị hủy vì một trận mưa như trút bất ngờ làm ngập bãi cỏ chỉ trong vài phút.
items.explanation:
A downpour is a sudden, very heavy fall of rain — the only option that could flood the lawn in minutes.
✗ drizzle — very light, fine rain; it could not flood anything; ✗ mist — thin fog hanging in the air, not falling rain; ✗ frost — a layer of ice on cold surfaces; no water to flood a lawn.

items.q: My brother has to ______ a decision about which career to follow before he finishes school.
items.vi: Anh trai tôi phải đưa ra quyết định về nghề nghiệp sẽ theo đuổi trước khi học xong.
items.explanation:
Make a decision is the fixed verb + noun collocation (= decide), and which career to follow shows a choice being made.
✗ do — 'do' goes with tasks and activities (do homework, do the dishes), never with 'decision'; ✗ have — 'have' collocates with a meal, a shower, a look, not with 'decision'; ✗ get — 'get' means receive or obtain; you cannot receive a decision you are making yourself.

items.q: Nam: Should I take the job in Da Nang or stay here? / Lan: ______ is that you need a steady income, so take it.
items.vi: Nam: Mình nên nhận việc ở Đà Nẵng hay ở lại đây? / Lan: Điều cốt lõi là cậu cần một nguồn thu nhập ổn định, nên nhận đi.
items.explanation:
The bottom line is the most important fact that decides a matter — here you need a steady income, so take it.
✗ the last straw — the final problem that makes you lose patience; ✗ the tip of the iceberg — a small visible part of a much bigger problem; ✗ the eleventh hour — the last possible moment before something happens. None of these states a deciding reason.

items.q: Lan: Why isn't Minh at school anymore? / Nam: He decided to ______ of school to help his father at the shop.
items.vi: Lan: Sao Minh không còn đi học nữa? / Nam: Cậu ấy quyết định bỏ học để phụ bố ở cửa hàng.
items.explanation:
Drop out of school means to leave school before finishing — the reason Minh isn't at school anymore — and it is the only option that takes of.
✗ drop off — fall asleep, or deliver someone somewhere; ✗ drop in — pay a short, casual visit (drop in on someone); ✗ drop by — call round briefly at a place; none combines with 'of school'.

items.q: You ______ such an expensive present; just coming to my birthday party was enough.
items.vi: Bạn không cần phải mua món quà đắt tiền như vậy đâu; chỉ cần đến dự sinh nhật mình là đủ rồi.
items.explanation:
Needn't have + past participle means something was done but was not necessary: the present was bought, and just coming was enough shows it wasn't needed.
✗ mustn't have bought — 'must have' only makes deductions, and its negative is 'can't have'; it never means 'it was unnecessary'; ✗ can't have bought — a deduction that something did NOT happen, but the present clearly exists; ✗ won't have bought — future perfect, for something finished by a future time.

items.q: Do you remember the year ______ our family first moved to Ho Chi Minh City?
items.vi: Bạn có nhớ năm mà gia đình chúng ta lần đầu chuyển đến Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh không?
items.explanation:
When is the relative adverb used after a time noun such as the year (= in which).
✗ where — refers to places, not times; ✗ whom — refers to people as an object; ✗ which — a pronoun that would need a preposition here: 'the year in which our family moved'.

items.q: Dad drove to work very slowly because of the thick ______ on the road this morning.
items.vi: Sáng nay bố lái xe đi làm rất chậm vì sương mù dày đặc trên đường.
items.explanation:
Fog is thick cloud near the ground that blocks a driver's view — the clue is thick … on the road making Dad drive slowly.
✗ hail — small balls of ice falling from the sky; it is not 'thick on the road'; ✗ thunder — the loud sound in a storm; it cannot be seen or be 'thick'; ✗ drought — a long period without rain, not something lying on a road.

items.q: By the time we got to Hoa's house, the party ______.
items.vi: Lúc chúng tôi đến nhà Hoa thì bữa tiệc đã bắt đầu rồi.
items.explanation:
By the time + past simple (got) marks a point in the past, and an action already complete before that point takes the past perfect: had already started.
✗ has already started — present perfect links to now, but the story is set in the past; ✗ was already starting — past continuous means it was only just beginning as we arrived, which clashes with 'already'; ✗ already starts — simple present cannot follow a past-time clause.

items.q: There isn't ______ milk left in the fridge, so could you buy some on the way home?
items.vi: Trong tủ lạnh không còn nhiều sữa, nên bạn mua thêm trên đường về nhà được không?
items.explanation:
Milk is an uncountable noun, and in a negative sentence (isn't) an uncountable noun takes much.
✗ many — only with plural countable nouns (many bottles); ✗ a few — plural countable nouns only, and 'isn't a few' is not used; ✗ few — also plural countable (few bottles) and already negative, so it cannot follow 'isn't'.

items.q: Put on your coat, or you will ______ a cold waiting for the bus in this wind.
items.vi: Mặc áo khoác vào đi, không thì bạn sẽ bị cảm lạnh khi đứng đợi xe buýt trong gió này.
items.explanation:
Catch a cold is the fixed collocation for becoming ill with a cold — the clue is the cold wind that makes you ill.
✗ take — 'take' collocates with medicine or a rest, not with an illness you get; ✗ hold — means keep something in your hand or position; nothing to do with getting ill; ✗ bring — means carry something to a place; you do not 'bring a cold'.

items.q: My aunt is used to ______ up early because she runs a stall at the market.
items.vi: Dì tôi đã quen với việc dậy sớm vì dì bán hàng ở chợ.
items.explanation:
Be used to (= be accustomed to) ends in the preposition 'to', so it takes a noun or -ing form: is used to getting up; the clue is is before 'used to'.
✗ get — a bare infinitive never follows a preposition; ✗ to get — the to-infinitive only follows 'used to' WITHOUT 'be', meaning a past habit (She used to get up early); ✗ got — a past form cannot follow 'to'.

items.q: My uncle's farm lost most of its rice this year because of the long ______.
items.vi: Nông trại của chú tôi mất gần hết lúa năm nay vì đợt hạn hán kéo dài.
items.explanation:
A drought is a long period without rain, which dries up crops — the clue is long plus a lost rice harvest.
✗ flood — too much water covering the land; it damages crops but is not described as 'long'; ✗ hail — balls of ice in a brief storm, not a long event; ✗ lightning — a sudden flash lasting a second; it cannot be 'long'.

items.q: Nam wants to become a doctor, ______ his twin brother dreams of opening a restaurant.
items.vi: Nam muốn trở thành bác sĩ, trong khi người anh sinh đôi của cậu ấy lại mơ mở một nhà hàng.
items.explanation:
Whereas is a conjunction that joins two contrasting clauses inside one sentence — Nam's plan versus his twin brother's different dream.
✗ however — an adverb, not a conjunction; it needs a full stop or semicolon before it ('…doctor. However, his…'); ✗ therefore — shows a result, but the second clause is a contrast, not a consequence; ✗ so that — shows purpose, but the brother's dream is not the purpose of Nam's plan.

items.q: Could you ______ my little sister from school today? I have a job interview at three.
items.vi: Hôm nay bạn đón em gái mình ở trường giúp được không? Mình có buổi phỏng vấn xin việc lúc ba giờ.
items.explanation:
Pick up someone from a place means to collect them, usually by car — the clue is from school.
✗ drop off — the opposite: leave someone AT a place; it goes with 'at', not 'from'; ✗ take up — start a hobby or activity (take up tennis); ✗ bring up — raise a child, or mention a topic in conversation.

items.q: If I ______ you, I would apply for the job at the new hotel before somebody else does.
items.vi: Nếu tôi là bạn, tôi sẽ nộp đơn xin việc ở khách sạn mới trước khi người khác nộp.
items.explanation:
The second conditional gives advice about an unreal present situation; would apply in the main clause tells you the if-clause needs a past form: If I were you, the fixed advice phrase.
✗ am — present simple belongs to the first conditional (If I am…, I will…), and 'I am you' is impossible; ✗ will be — 'will' is not used in the if-clause of a conditional; ✗ had been — third conditional, which would need 'would have applied'.

items.q: Lan: I want to save up for a new laptop. / Nam: Then you'll have to ______ and stop buying bubble tea every day.
items.vi: Lan: Mình muốn để dành tiền mua laptop mới. / Nam: Vậy thì cậu phải thắt lưng buộc bụng và ngừng mua trà sữa mỗi ngày.
items.explanation:
Tighten your belt means to spend less money because you have less to spend — the clue is save up and stop buying bubble tea.
✗ hold your horses — wait, slow down, don't rush; ✗ keep your chin up — stay cheerful in a difficult time; ✗ bite your tongue — stop yourself from saying something. None of these is about money.

items.q: The invitations for the party ______ to all our classmates yesterday.
items.vi: Thiệp mời dự tiệc đã được gửi tới tất cả các bạn cùng lớp hôm qua.
items.explanation:
The invitations cannot send themselves, so the passive is needed, and yesterday fixes the past simple: were sent.
✗ sent — active past simple, which would make the invitations the sender; ✗ have been sent — present perfect passive cannot combine with a finished past time like 'yesterday'; ✗ are sent — present simple passive describes a habit or general fact, not one completed event yesterday.

items.q: After the rain stopped, a bright ______ stretched across the sky above our house.
items.vi: Sau khi mưa tạnh, một chiếc cầu vồng rực rỡ trải dài trên bầu trời phía trên nhà chúng tôi.
items.explanation:
A rainbow is the coloured arc that appears when the sun comes out after the rain — the only option that stretches across the sky.
✗ thunder — the loud noise in a storm; it is heard, not seen; ✗ lightning — a sudden flash DURING a storm, not after the rain stops; ✗ hail — small balls of ice that fall, not something stretched across the sky.

items.q: Mai said that she ______ her grandparents in the countryside the following weekend.
items.vi: Mai nói rằng cô ấy sẽ về thăm ông bà ở quê vào cuối tuần sau đó.
items.explanation:
After a past reporting verb (said) the tense shifts back, so 'will visit' becomes would visit; the following weekend (the reported form of 'next weekend') confirms it.
✗ will visit — 'will' stays only after a present reporting verb (says); ✗ visits — present simple describes a habit, not a plan for one future weekend; ✗ has visited — present perfect means the visit is already done, but 'the following weekend' is still to come.

items.q: My cousins are going to ______ a party for Grandma's seventieth birthday next month.
items.vi: Các anh chị họ của tôi sẽ tổ chức một bữa tiệc mừng sinh nhật lần thứ bảy mươi của bà vào tháng sau.
items.explanation:
Throw a party (also have/hold/give a party) is the collocation for organising a celebration, and for Grandma's birthday shows one being organised.
✗ make — 'make' is for producing things (make a cake), not events; ✗ do — 'do' is for tasks and chores (do the shopping), not for parties; ✗ put — needs 'on' to mean organise (put on a show); alone it is meaningless here.

items.q: My father ______ at the same bank since he left college, and he still enjoys it.
items.vi: Bố tôi đã làm việc ở cùng một ngân hàng kể từ khi rời trường cao đẳng, và bố vẫn thích công việc đó.
items.explanation:
Since + a past starting point (since he left college) with a situation that continues now (still enjoys it) takes the present perfect: has worked.
✗ works — simple present describes the habit but cannot go with 'since'; ✗ is working — present continuous describes a temporary action now, not a period running from the past; ✗ worked — past simple means the job is over, but he still enjoys it.

items.q: At the class reunion, I finally had time to catch up ______ my old friends.
items.vi: Ở buổi họp lớp, cuối cùng tôi cũng có thời gian hàn huyên với bạn bè cũ.
items.explanation:
Catch up with someone means to meet them and exchange news — the clue is my old friends at a reunion.
✗ on — 'catch up on' goes with things you missed (catch up on sleep, homework), not people; ✗ to — 'catch up to' means physically reach someone ahead of you, not chat; ✗ at — 'catch up at' is not a phrasal verb in English.

items.q: Check the weather ______ before you invite everyone to the beach on Sunday.
items.vi: Hãy xem dự báo thời tiết trước khi mời mọi người đi biển vào Chủ nhật.
items.explanation:
A weather forecast is a prediction of the coming weather — what you check before planning a beach trip on Sunday.
✗ climate — the usual weather of a region over many years; it cannot be 'checked' for one Sunday; ✗ temperature — only how hot or cold it is, and 'weather temperature' is not a phrase; ✗ season — a part of the year (summer, winter), not something you check for a day.

items.q: Living in the city is ______ more expensive than living in our hometown, so I might move back after graduation.
items.vi: Sống ở thành phố đắt đỏ hơn nhiều so với sống ở quê, nên có lẽ tôi sẽ chuyển về sau khi tốt nghiệp.
items.explanation:
A comparative (more expensive) is strengthened with far, much or a lot; the clue is more … than around the adjective.
✗ very — modifies a plain adjective (very expensive), never a comparative; ✗ too — means 'more than enough' with a plain adjective (too expensive); ✗ so — goes with a plain adjective (so expensive) or 'so … that', not with 'more … than'.
